round-8 finding #4 (round-7 carry, confirmed 2/2) FIXED: the no-unkeyed-Ledger enumeration perimeter was regex-permeable. The pattern (?<![\w.])Ledger\( has a negative lookbehind that EXCLUDES a preceding dot, so a module-qualified construction (manifest.Ledger() and an aliased import (import Ledger as L; L()) evaded it entirely, and the chain_key= check was a fragile 240-char substring window. Replaced with an AST perimeter (_target_call_nodes) that resolves the symbol through direct/aliased/qualified/defining-module bindings and reads the actual call keywords. Generalized and applied to BOTH the Ledger construction enumeration AND the identical decide_promotion single-caller enumeration in the same file (same permeability class, closed in the same sweep rather than left as a matching hole). Stated residual: a dynamic getattr construction is outside the static perimeter (a reviewable event). Forcing test tests/test_chain_key.py::test_the_enumeration_perimeter_catches_aliased_and_qualified_construction proves each exact evasion is now SEEN and its key-threading reported truthfully.
